slides.title: Tactile Sensors Are an Effective Substitute for Wrist Cameras in Contact-Rich or Occluded Manipulation
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that finger-mounted tactile sensors can significantly outperform wrist cameras in contact-rich manipulation tasks, offering a robust alternative for handling occlusions and establishing precise contacts. This aligns with MOSAIC's focus on integrating physics and force-based feedback to estimate procedural skill and enhance human-AI coadaptation in assembly tasks.

card.one_liner: Finger-mounted tactile sensors effectively substitute for wrist cameras in contact-rich or occluded manipulation tasks.
card.key_idea: Integrates low-cost tactile arrays into an ACT policy, replacing wrist-camera inputs with tactile maps processed via a shared ResNet-18 backbone.
card.evaluation: Tested on six real-world tasks with 1,000 rollouts; tactile-only policies outperformed wrist-camera vision-only policies on three contact-rich tasks.
card.limitation: Results rely on a single robot platform, one tactile sensor type, one policy architecture, and a fixed training seed.

slides.title: Which Taxels, Not How Many: Tactile Sensor Placement for Dexterous Policies
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that strategically selecting tactile sensors based on contact statistics can match the performance of dense uniform arrays, offering insights into efficient multimodal sensing design relevant to resource-constrained perception systems.

card.one_liner: Tactile sensor placement based on contact statistics outperforms uniform placement with fewer taxels.
card.key_idea: Selecting taxels via teacher contact statistics (Top-contact/Contact-cover) matches large uniform sets; tensor layout is irrelevant.
card.evaluation: Simulated in-palm rotation and grasping on three robot hands using teacher-student distillation; measured success rate and held fraction.
card.limitation: Results are simulation-only, ignoring real-world sensor noise and drift; conclusions may not transfer directly to physical hardware.

slides.title: MDF++: Visuo-Tactile World Action Model with End-to-end Representation Learning
slides.highlight: This work introduces MDF++, a visuo-tactile world-action model that learns control-relevant representations end-to-end using a diffusion backbone, outperforming models with frozen encoders by up to 50% on contact-rich manipulation tasks.

card.one_liner: MDF++ learns task-aware visuo-tactile representations via selective gradient flow, outperforming frozen encoders in contact-rich manipulation.
card.key_idea: End-to-end training of observation encoders with a diffusion backbone using cross-modal prediction and selective gradient flow to prevent feature collapse.
card.evaluation: Tested on 5 simulated and 2 real-world threading tasks; outperforms frozen-encoder baselines by up to 50% in success rate.
card.limitation: Requires manual loss weight tuning per modality and processes force signals at low frequency, potentially missing high-frequency dynamics.

slides.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a tactile foundation model that unifies heterogeneous sensor data, enabling plug-and-play integration into vision-language-action policies to enhance dexterity in contact-rich manipulation tasks.

card.one_liner: LingBot-Touch creates a unified tactile representation across diverse sensors to enhance dexterous manipulation policies.
card.key_idea: Develops a tactile foundation model generating unified, plug-and-play tokens from heterogeneous sensors for diffusion and VLA policies.
card.evaluation: Validated via simulation and real-robot tests on multiple platforms, showing improved dexterity and efficiency across various policies.

slides.title: GUARD: Anomaly-Informed Q-Steering for Generative Robot Policies in Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a method to steer generative robot policies using anomaly signals derived from training data, offering a non-data-hungry approach to robustness that aligns with HyECHO's goal of efficient multimodal perception.

card.one_liner: GUARD steers generative robot policies using anomaly-informed Q-functions to prevent covariate shift failures.
card.key_idea: Combines sparse task rewards with dense anomaly scores from training data into a Q-function, whose gradients steer flow-matching denoising.
card.evaluation: Tested on Adroit simulation and real Allegro hand; achieves 96% success, outperforming baselines by ~21pp with strong sim-to-real transfer.
card.limitation: Requires online interaction for Q-function adaptation and relies on accurate anomaly detection from the policy's training distribution.

slides.title: Robust Readout of Cross-Point Resistive Arrays via Time-Domain Optimization
slides.tldr: TIME-DOMAIN OPTIMIZATION FOR ROBUST TACTILE SENSING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a time-domain optimization method for cross-point resistive arrays that significantly improves readout accuracy in noisy robotic sensing environments compared to conventional frequency-based approaches.

card.one_liner: Time-domain optimization improves robustness of cross-point resistive array readout against noise compared to frequency methods.
card.key_idea: Fits time-domain observation models to measured waveforms via nonlinear least-squares, avoiding reliance on spectral amplitudes.
card.evaluation: Simulated 16x16 arrays in LTspice; reduced mean error by 20% and standard deviation by 77.6% under noise vs FFT baseline.
card.limitation: Higher computational cost due to iterative optimization; ignores sneak-path currents in cross-point arrays.

slides.title: PCTac: Mechanochromic Photonic-Crystal Tactile Sensor for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: PCTac introduces an open-source mechanochromic photonic-crystal fingertip that encodes local stress as a spatially resolved hue field, offering a direct physical representation of force for robot learning. Integrating this hue-based observation into a Diffusion Policy significantly outperforms standard RGB tactile and vision-only baselines in real-world dexterous manipulation tasks.

card.one_liner: PCTac uses mechanochromic photonic crystals to encode contact stress directly as hue for dexterous robot manipulation.
card.key_idea: A tactile fingertip converts local stress into structural color changes, using a reference-relative hue field as a direct policy observation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three real-robot tasks with Diffusion Policy; PCTac Hue achieved 75.6% success, outperforming RGB and vision-only baselines.
card.limitation: Low sensitivity to concave features and ambiguity between normal and shear loads due to limited elastomer conformability.

slides.title: Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids (DASH): Latency-Agnostic Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models for Humanoid Manipulation
slides.highlight: DASH decouples vision-language backbones from action heads to maintain high control rates in humanoid manipulation, addressing latency bottlenecks relevant to embodied robot systems.

card.one_liner: DASH decouples VLA backbones from control loops, enabling latency-agnostic scaling for high-frequency humanoid manipulation.
card.key_idea: Splits policy into slow VLM and fast flow-matching head via LCM; fuses stale semantics with fresh vision using desynchronized training.
card.evaluation: RoboTwin simulation (0.8B-8B backbones) and real humanoid pick-and-place; shows 20Hz control rate and higher success than synchronous baselines.
card.limitation: Evaluated primarily on quasi-static tasks; performance on dynamic, long-horizon scenarios remains unverified.
